# Citation

Huang, W., et al. (2012). *ART: a next-generation sequencing read simulator*. Bioinformatics. DOI: 10.1093/bioinformatics/btr708. Source: [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3278762/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3278762/).

# One-Sentence Summary

Introduces ART, a simulator for next-generation sequencing reads with technology-specific empirical error profiles.

# Scope for simitall

Use as the short-read backend in simitall hybrid-assembly workflows. Record the ART profile, read length, insert distribution, coverage, and random seed as required provenance.

# Agent-Safe Takeaways

- Illumina simulation requires a platform profile, paired-end configuration, read length, insert distribution, and coverage.
- Read-level errors affect assembly and variant-calling benchmarks.
- Simulation parameters must be reported to make an assembly benchmark reproducible.

# Inputs to Specify

- Reference FASTA
- Sequencing-system profile
- Read length, paired-end insert model, coverage, and seed

# Expected Outputs

- FASTQ reads
- Tool log and parameter record

# Limitations and Guardrails

- An empirical error profile does not represent every instrument, library preparation, or batch effect.
- Do not equate nominal coverage with effective genome coverage without QC.

# Questions This Record Can Ground

- Which parameters are essential for a paired-end ART simulation?
- What provenance should accompany synthetic Illumina reads?
